title: Small solution sets on a set-generated localizing derived subcategory
statement: Let A be a Grothendieck abelian category with Hom sets and derived category D(A) in the morphism universe v [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let P be a v-essentially small class in D(A). Let Q be a replete triangulated full subcategory closed under all v-indexed coproducts, containing P, and minimal among subcategories with these properties. For every cohomological functor H:Q^op to Ab_v carrying v-indexed coproducts to products, there is a v-small family of pairs (B_i,b_i in H(B_i)) through which every element z in H(Z) pulls back along some Z to B_i. No uniqueness or representing object is asserted.

source.place: Well-generation and solution-set construction in the Brown step: Neeman Theorem 0.2; Krause Localization theory 7.2.1 and 5.1.1, and Derived categories, resolutions, and Brown representability 4.5.

proof.text: Neeman, On the derived category of sheaves on a manifold, Theorem 0.2, gives well generation of D(A). Choose a small family representing P and a common uncountable regular cardinal for which these objects and the ambient generators are alpha-compact.

Krause, Localization theory for triangulated categories, Theorem 7.2.1, takes the alpha-localizing closure of the small family to obtain small alpha-small perfect generators for its localizing hull. Containment and minimality identify this hull with Q.

Use the cellular construction for perfect generators in Krause, Derived categories, resolutions, and Brown representability, Section 4.5 (equivalently the construction behind Localization theory 5.1.1). Start with all H-elements on shifted generators, iteratively kill generator maps in the kernel by distinguished triangles and lift the elements by cohomological exactness. Take the sequential telescope and lift the compatible elements using the product hypothesis. In the abelian category of coherent functors on the additive closure of the perfect family, perfectness identifies the restricted telescope with the appropriate colimit of stages. The universal transformation is an isomorphism on the generators and their shifts; the class on which it is an isomorphism is localizing, hence all of Q. Retain only its surjectivity to obtain the required family. All indexing sets use universe v.

theorem setGeneratedDerived_cohomological_solutionSet
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{v} A]
    (P Q : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory A))
    [ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.{v} P]
    [Q.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] [Q.IsTriangulated]
    [∀ I : Type v, Q.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)]
    (hP : P ≤ Q)
    (hminimal : ∀ R : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory A), P ≤ R →
      R.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms → R.IsTriangulated →
      (∀ I : Type v, R.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)) → Q ≤ R)
    (H : Q.FullSubcategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v}) [H.IsHomological]
    (hH : ∀ I : Type v, PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) H) :
    ∃ (I : Type v) (B : I → Q.FullSubcategory) (b : ∀ i, H.obj (op (B i))),
      ∀ (Z : Q.FullSubcategory) (z : H.obj (op Z)), ∃ (i : I) (f : Z ⟶ B i),
        H.map f.op (b i) = z
